script: It's one of the most confusing, and honestly grossest, behaviors dogs do, and yet it's surprisingly common, especially in puppies. There are actually several real explanations behind it. Some puppies do it simply out of curiosity, exploring the world with their mouth the same way they explore everything else. Mother dogs also clean up after their puppies in the den by doing exactly this, so young puppies sometimes copy behavior they've literally watched their mother do. In adult dogs, it can be tied to an underlying nutrient deficiency, certain diets that are lower quality or harder to digest can leave stool smelling more appealing than it should, from a dog's perspective. Stress, boredom, or being kept in a space that isn't cleaned frequently enough can also make the behavior more likely to start or continue. In rare cases it's linked to a genuine digestive or pancreatic issue, which is worth ruling out with a vet if the behavior is new or frequent in an adult dog. The good news is it's almost always manageable, consistent cleanup, a quality diet, and enough mental stimulation solve it for the vast majority of dogs. It looks alarming, but it's rarely as serious as it seems.
